legacy_root.answer: Hooks consume a UTF-8 JSON object on stdin (session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, permission_mode, plus event-specific fields). Exit 2 is reserved for irreversible danger on PreToolUse/PermissionRequest with a typed danger claim; every other guidance injects additionalContext and cannot block. Internal errors and timeouts fail open (session continues, process exit 0). Wiring is proven only when a live invocation produces both a dispatcher fire record and a hook-written side effect; a file on disk is not proof. SUCCESS:ARC-0088

consumer_call_site.role: loads the draft and asserts event types, stdin fields, and two-signal wiring

reconstructed_from: catalog/sibling event names (PostToolUse, Notification, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PermissionRequest, ...)

exit_code_semantics.exit_0: hook completed; optional additionalContext is injected; session continues
exit_code_semantics.exit_2: block the pending action; allowed only for irreversible danger on blocking events
exit_code_semantics.other_nonzero: treated as internal error: fail open, process exit coerced to 0

fail_open.on_internal_error: Uncaught exception, spawn failure, invalid stdin, or any non-zero exit other than a valid danger-backed exit 2 is coerced to process exit 0 with session_continue=true.

honesty.no_host_client_invocation: This contract is executed against the in-tree dispatcher, not against a live host-client session on this Linux worktree.
honesty.user_prompts_slice: ABSENT; event list reconstructed from on-disk hook fixtures plus sibling catalog names

inject_do_not_block.rule: Advisory output (style, budget, unknown tool, missing context, linter, secret-scan advisory) is injected as additionalContext and must never produce exit 2.

legacy_root.question: Specify the hook contract: event types, the stdin JSON input shape, exit-code semantics with exit 2 reserved for irreversible danger only, the inject-do-not-block rule for all other guidance, the mandatory fail-open behaviour on internal error, the timeout, and the registration record that PROVES a hook is actually wired rather than merely present as a file.

stdin_json_shape.delivery: single UTF-8 JSON object on stdin; no argv payload

timeout.on_timeout: kill the hook, fail open, inject a timeout notice if any

legacy_root.title: Contract: Hook contract: IO, exit-code semantics, fail-open requirement and wiring proof

wiring_proof.both_states: unregister (file remains) => wired=false; re-register and invoke => both signals fire and wired=true
wiring_proof.wired_iff: dispatcher_record_observed AND side_effect_observed after a live invocation; manifest_present and file_present are recorded and never sufficient
